newsitem.title: USA: Harkin urges White House to "hold firm" on ethanol.
newsitem.headline: Harkin urges White House to "hold firm" on ethanol.

text.p: Senator Tom Harkin Friday urged the Clinton Adminstration to hold firm on its committment to extend the ethanol tax break during tax negotiations with Congressional Republicans.

"The president should make certain that common sense will prevail in these tax negotiations," the Iowa Democrat said in a letter to President Clinton. "Ethanol has the facts on its side and many senators on its side."
The Clinton administration has backed extending the subsidy for the corn-based fuel until the year 2007.

House and Senate Republicans did not settle on an ethanol provision when they drafted their unified tax proposal, leaving the controversial issue to be settled at the negotiating table with the White House.
Senate tax legislation extended the subsidy until the year 2007, paring it down modestly in that period. The House bill left the subsidy intact but ended it as scheduled in the year 2000.
